subject: S.U.R.E. — Autonomous Sturgeon Welfare Monitoring in RAS via Edge-AI and RAG-Enhanced Deterministic Fusion

novel_claims.claim: A dependency-free deterministic rule engine (backend/rules.py) as the sole source of truth for safety severity, with escalate-only precedence over an LLM's severity judgment, enforced by literal code-sharing between the production decision path and the evaluation harness, with the escalate-only merge (backend/main.py::apply_rule_override) additionally shown to be unit-tested for logical soundness under synthetic fixtures (backend/test_decision.py) — distinct from, and not yet substituted for, behavioral evidence of what the LLM emits in practice.
novel_claims.closest_prior_work: LLM-as-advisor-with-deterministic-override patterns in fintech and medical triage; constitutional-AI and output-validator guardrail approaches. These typically re-validate LLM output via a second model or a schema/format check rather than a domain-specific rule engine with formal escalation-only precedence semantics and code-level identity between eval and production paths.

novel_claims.claim: Deterministic (non-LLM) agentic tool routing was adopted specifically because a benchmark (agent/bench_agent.py) demonstrated the target-scale on-device LLM (AQUA-1B, Gemma 3 1B) fails to reliably emit parseable, correctly-selected tool-call actions (0% format, 0% selection across scripted scenarios; identical output under a prefill test), and the benchmark's own constant-answer-detection technique (flagging a selection percentage as an artifact when the model emits the same tool choice across ≥3 scenarios, rather than trusting the aggregate) is itself a small, transferable evaluation-methodology contribution, separable from the negative result it uncovered.
novel_claims.novelty_type: negative result / evidence-driven architectural decision, plus a secondary evaluation-methodology contribution
novel_claims.closest_prior_work: General agentic tool-use / function-calling benchmarks (e.g., ToolBench-style evaluations) assess format compliance and tool selection in the abstract; this system is a rarer case of such a benchmark result being the documented, causal justification for abandoning LLM-driven routing in a shipped, safety-critical production architecture rather than remaining an isolated academic finding. The constant-answer-detection check is a lightweight, generalizable safeguard against overreading an aggregate tool-selection percentage that most published benchmarks do not apply.

novel_claims.claim: RAG similarity-threshold selection driven by an explicit positive/hard-negative sweep and an asymmetric cost function, shipping a non-F1-optimal threshold (0.85, F1 0.906) over the F1-optimal threshold (0.84, F1 0.951) to drive fabricated-citation pass-through to exactly zero.
novel_claims.closest_prior_work: Precision-biased similarity thresholding to reduce RAG hallucination is a known idea in RAG-safety literature generally. The specific instantiation here — an explicit hard-negative sweep (not just held-out positives), a stated asymmetric-cost justification (missed document vs. fabricated citation), and application in a safety-critical agricultural/industrial domain — is a tighter, more transparently justified version of the general idea rather than a novel mechanism.

novel_claims.claim: Diagnosis and correction of a Population Stability Index (PSI) drift-detection failure mode: equal-width binning over [0,1] produces a degenerate binary alarm (PSI 0.06 -> 1.05 with no gradient) when detection confidences are concentrated in a narrow empirical band, corrected by quantile-edge (decile) binning that yields a graded signal (0.039 -> 0.098 -> 0.265 -> 8.28) across increasing synthetic degradation; retraining is further gated by a MIN_IMPROVEMENT (0.005 mAP50) bar against training-noise deltas.
novel_claims.closest_prior_work: PSI computed over model output distributions (rather than input features) for drift monitoring is established industry MLOps practice (e.g., credit-risk and fraud-model monitoring). The novel element is the diagnosis of *why* equal-width binning fails under narrow-band confidence distributions and the resulting quantile-binning fix, not the underlying use of PSI itself; the MIN_IMPROVEMENT retrain gate is a straightforward decision-theoretic addition rather than a novel statistical method.

novel_claims.claim: A single, coherent 'deterministic authority over probabilistic components' design philosophy applied and independently tested at four architecturally distinct layers (decision, agent/tool-routing, retrieval, MLOps retraining) within one deployed applied system, including at least one full disclosed negative result used as design evidence.
novel_claims.closest_prior_work: No identified prior applied-systems paper argues this pattern as a unifying cross-layer thesis with a disclosed negative result at more than one layer. Closest analogues address guardrails, deterministic overrides, or drift detection at a single layer in isolation (e.g., LLM output validation alone, or MLOps drift monitoring alone) without a cross-layer consistency argument or a negative-result component.

novel_claims.claim: NEW ROUND 2 — a systematic, toolchain-diagnosed export-format accuracy loss in a YOLOv11s edge-deployment pipeline: ONNX and TorchScript CPU exports match each other's mAP50/precision loss to four decimal places relative to the fp32/MPS baseline (implicating a shared post-processing/NMS path, not per-format numeric precision), and INT8 quantization on top of ONNX shows a *smaller* mAP50 delta (-0.0082) than the fp32 export path already pays (-0.0104) before quantization is applied — falsifying 'quantization is where you pay for edge speed' as applied to this pipeline, while CoreML/ANE dominates on latency (p50 9.0ms/111FPS) without a larger accuracy cost.
novel_claims.closest_prior_work: CoreML/ANE and Jetson-class latency benchmarking of YOLO-family detectors is common, but most public benchmarks report speed without re-measuring accuracy per export target, and none identified attribute a shared cross-format accuracy loss to a common post-processing path rather than to per-format numeric precision or to quantization specifically. This is a toolchain-specific diagnosis, not a claim about ONNX/TorchScript export correctness in general.

novel_claims.claim: NEW ROUND 2 — an explicit trace from a vision detector's chosen precision/recall operating point (0.858/0.719) to the single deterministic rule that consumes its output (backend/rules.py's fish_count == 0 check), showing that rule triggers on total per-frame absence rather than per-instance detection misses, and disclosing that the ~28% per-instance miss rate the recall figure measures is therefore not directly gated by any current safety rule — closing a 'so what' gap between a standalone vision benchmark number and the system's actual safety architecture.
novel_claims.closest_prior_work: Precision/recall reporting for detector-based monitoring systems is standard; explicitly tracing a specific recall figure through to the exact downstream rule-trigger semantics that consume it, and disclosing the resulting coverage gap rather than assuming proportional safety coverage, is not a common practice in applied precision-aquaculture or precision-livestock vision papers reviewed to date.

unresolved_gaps_tracked_as_research_goal: AQUA-1B has never been run through llm-service/eval.py in model mode. Rewritten in Round 2 with zero blocking dependency (adapter and model weights already cached locally) and a precisely specified fix: eval.py's model_status() never calls backend/main.py's apply_rule_override, so the run must be paired with a separate pass of parsed model output through apply_rule_override (or eval.py must be extended to call it) to actually measure the paper's central escalated-severity claim, classified into a FOUR-bucket taxonomy as of Round 3 (agrees / under-calls-and-escalated / over-calls / unparseable-defaulted-to-ok) — the over-calls bucket was added in Round 3 per Rigor's finding that apply_rule_override only ever escalates, never downgrades, so a model over-call had no representable outcome in the prior three-bucket scheme.

twin_bridge/ independent PLC (CODESYS/IEC 61131-3) cross-validation module exists in the codebase but has zero produced results; the previously proposed fallback ('generate a session from an existing recorded demo') referenced a nonexistent artifact. Rescoped this round into two separated claims: (a) backend/test_decision.py and twin_bridge/test_bridge.py already provide unit-tested mechanism-correctness evidence, usable now and explicitly labeled as not a substitute for field validation; (b) a live compare.py --watch/--replay session is an honestly-scoped stretch goal with a dated go/no-go checkpoint and a pre-committed three-outcome interpretation plan (full agreement / explicable divergence / unexplained divergence), not claimed as 'independently validated' unless actually executed.

RAG threshold sweep is published as only two points (0.84, 0.85); the full sweep from rag/calibrate.py has not been recovered to confirm 0.84 is the true F1-argmax. Confirmed low-risk, no infrastructure gap (Rigor, Round 2).
Synthetic-only validation of PSI drift-gating; no field-observed production drift episode has been reported.

Small sample sizes throughout: 29 RAG queries / 12 hard negatives, 40 edge-latency frames on a single device, agent benchmark, 98-image validation split. Round 2 proposed bench_agent.py's --repeat flag as a zero-cost sample-size fix for the agent benchmark; Round 3 Rigor traced the code and found this factually wrong (make_generator() runs at temp=0.0 by explicit design, so --repeat produces byte-identical, non-independent copies, not new samples). The claim is retracted; the honest path is either authoring genuinely new, distinct scenarios before manuscript freeze, or stating the n=5-scenario/2-model benchmark as a disclosed limitation rather than an addressed concern.

LoRA adapter provenance ambiguity: deployed adapter may still be the 8-sample v1 rather than the untested 128-sample v2 — now tracked as a zero-cost sub-step of the eval.py goal (file mtime / git log check) rather than a standalone caveat.
